newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rodamco sees profit boost from French buy.
newsitem.headline: Rodamco sees profit boost from French buy.

text.p: Rodamco NV said on Friday its takeover of French property fund Cegep, which was finalised today, was expected to boost its net profits.

"Because the transaction will be financed from our liquid assets, the direct positive effect on Rodamco NV's net profit will be about 32 million guilders per year from the financial year 1997/98," the property arm of the Robeco group of investment funds said in a statement.
The effect in the current year will be limited to 13 million guilders. Rodamco said it maintained its previous forecast that 1996/97's net profit would be slightly lower than last year's.
This year's positive effect of the Cegep takeover will be offset by negative impacts of currency changes, it added. In 1995/96 Rodamco posted a full-year net of 446 million guilders.
Rodamco said earlier today it would pay a total of about 1.75 billion francs for Cegep's outstanding shares and convertible bonds.

Rodamco said it will also refinance Cegep's outstanding bank loans and tax obligations, which will raise its total investment in the French firm to 2.35 billion francs. Rodamco said Cegep's interests in shopping centres had a value of 2.40 billion francs and its other assets were worth another 200 million francs.
The Cegep takeover increases Rodamco's investments in French shops to a total value of about four billion francs. Rodamco's group assets currently total about 8.3 billion guilders.
In the first six months of 1996/97 to August 31, Rodamco's net profit fell by 14 million guilders to 210 million. The group said this was mainly caused by higher interest charges.
Net rental income remained virtually unchanged, despite the sale of some investments by the end of last year.
